days.topic: Lesson 5: Flower, Fruits and Seeds · Fruits and Fleshy Fruits
days.title: Which fleshy fruit?

items.w: One seed in a stony endocarp, with a fleshy mesocarp.
Stony pit (endocarp) around one seed: a drupe.
Like cherry and peach: one seed, stony endocarp.
A drupe with a fibrous mesocarp (the husk).
The whole ovary wall is juicy: a berry.
Botanically a berry: juicy ovary wall.
A berry: fleshy ovary wall with many seeds.
A true berry, as the name says (juicy ovary wall).
A pepo: a berry with a hard rind.
Hard rind around a fleshy inside: pepo.
Pepo, like squash and watermelon.
A pepo: hard rind (gourd family).

days.topic: Chapter 11: Personality: Theory and Measurement · The Psychodynamic Perspective
days.title: Whose idea is it?

items.w: Freud's three structures of the mind.
Freud: oral, anal, phallic, latency, genital.
Freud: the automatic ejection of anxiety-evoking ideas.
Jung: a store of human experience we all share.
Jung: inherited images in the collective unconscious.
The name of Jung's school.
Adler: feeling inferior drives the striving for superiority.
Adler: we shape our own personality.
The name of Adler's school.
Rogers: valued as a person, whatever the behavior.
Rogers: the self-concept close to the self-ideal.
Rogers: standards others use to judge our value.

days.topic: Lesson 6: Plant Kingdom · Plant Characteristics and Classification
days.title: Which plant group?

items.w: An alga: a thallus with no true roots, stems or leaves.
Sea lettuce, an alga eaten as food.
A brown alga: thallophyte.
A liverwort: bryophyte, no vascular tissue.
A moss: bryophyte.
Peat moss: bryophyte.
A heterosporous pteridophyte (seedless vascular).
Horsetail: seedless vascular plant.
A fern: pteridophyte.
A cycad: naked seeds in cones.
Pine, a conifer: naked seeds.
A gymnosperm with naked seeds.

days.topic: Chapter 12: Stress, Health, and Coping · Stress and the Body
days.title: Which stage of the GAS?

items.w: The alarm reaction is the fight-or-flight response.
Alarm: the sympathetic nervous system fires up.
In the alarm reaction the adrenal medulla releases adrenaline (book).
Resistance: arousal stays high while the body adapts.
Resistance: long arousal weakens the immune system.
Selye also called the resistance stage the adaptation stage.
Exhaustion: the parasympathetic system may take over.
Exhaustion is when diseases of adaptation appear.

days.title: Fleshy, or dry and opens?

items.w: Fleshy, with a stony endocarp.
Fleshy: juicy ovary wall.
Fleshy with a leathery rind (orange, lemon).
Fleshy accessory fruit (apple, pear).
Dry dehiscent: opens along both sutures (pea, bean).
Dry dehiscent: opens along one suture.
Dry dehiscent, from several carpels.
Dry dehiscent: long, 2 carpels (mustard).
Dry indehiscent: one seed attached at one point.
Dry indehiscent and winged (maple, elm).
Dry indehiscent: the grain (seed coat fused to pericarp).
A nut: dry indehiscent with a very hard wall.
Paracetamol + phenylephrine.
Paracetamol + phenylephrine + chlorphenamine.
Paracetamol + dextromethorphan + phenylpropanolamine.
Paracetamol + caffeine.
Ibuprofen, a propionic acid ("pro" drug).
Ibuprofen: propionic acid.
Naproxen, a propionic acid.
Mefenamic acid, a fenamate.
Mefenamic acid: fenamate.

days.topic: Lesson 7: Anti-Inflammatory Drugs · Inflammation, Prostanoids, Pain and Fever
days.title: COX-1, COX-2 or LOX?

items.w: COX-1 is constitutive: the housekeeping enzyme.
COX-1 keeps the stomach lining protected.
COX-1 housekeeping includes kidney blood flow.
Thromboxane A2 comes from COX-1.
COX-2 shows up when called: inducible by inflammation.
COX-2 makes prostanoids for inflammation and cancer.
Coxibs are COX-2 selective.
L for LOX and leukotrienes.
Leukotrienes from LOX drive allergy and asthma.
Montelukast blocks leukotrienes.

days.topic: Topic 12: Aromatic Compounds (Hydrocarbons II) · Directing Effects and Synthesis
days.title: Where does the next group go?

items.w: An electron-donating group: ortho/para director, ring reacts faster than benzene.
An electron-donating group: ortho/para director, ring reacts faster.
–OR is electron-donating: ortho/para director.
Alkyl groups donate electrons: ortho/para, so toluene is faster than benzene.
Halogens are the exception: electron-withdrawing, yet still ortho/para.
Halogens are the exception: electron-withdrawing, yet still ortho/para.
Electron-withdrawing: directs meta and slows the ring (nitrobenzene is slower).
A carbonyl group is electron-withdrawing: meta director.
Electron-withdrawing: meta director.
A carbonyl group (C=O) is electron-withdrawing: meta director.

days.topic: Chapter 12: Stress, Health, and Coping · Psychological Moderators of Stress
days.title: Whose idea about stress?

items.w: Selye named healthful stress eustress.
Selye: illnesses like allergies and heart disease after prolonged stress.
Selye's three-stage response of the body to any stressor.
Shelley Taylor: under stress, women tend to nurture and seek support.
Taylor's response, mainly in women, in place of fight or flight.
Albert Ellis: unrealistic beliefs make events stressful.
Ellis: Activating event, Belief, Consequence.
B in Ellis's A-B-C stands for beliefs about the event.
Kobasa's three characteristics of psychological hardiness.
Our understanding of hardiness comes mainly from Suzanne Kobasa.

days.topic: Topic 3: Health Awareness · Dengue, Malaria, Cholera
days.title: Which disease?

items.w: Dengue virus belongs to the genus Flavivirus.
Dengue is caused by one of four closely related virus serotypes.
The dengue virus belongs to the family Flaviviridae.
Malaria is spread by the female Anopheles mosquito.
The most serious malaria parasite.

items.t: Symptoms up to a year later
items.w: Malaria symptoms begin from a week up to a year after infection.
A cholera sign, with low blood pressure, thirst and weight loss.
Cholera incubates from less than one day to five days.
Typhoid fever is most often caused by Salmonella typhi.
A typhoid sign, with enlarged liver and spleen.
Typhoid signs: coated tongue, enlarged liver and spleen, rash.
